title: How We Built This Coding Style With a GPT Agent and an External Reviewer

cover.alt: Conceptual dual-view inspection of the same website model, representing building and independent review.

figures.title: One build, two viewpoints
figures.summary: The review loop starts from rendered behavior and feeds concrete fixes back into implementation.

items.label: Build in the repo
items.detail: The coding agent edits the implementation.

items.label: Run the site
items.detail: The local server exposes the actual rendered pages.

items.label: Review externally
items.detail: The reviewer inspects the page as a visitor would.

items.label: Scope the finding
items.detail: Name the page, section, problem, and proposed fix.

items.label: Fix and verify
items.detail: Apply a narrow change and rerun checks.

figures.caption: A schematic of the workflow described in this article, not a claim of autonomous quality assurance.

figures.title: A finding that can become a fix
figures.summary: Specific feedback reduces the translation required between review and implementation.

items.label: What is broken?
items.detail: Describe the present behavior, such as overlap or an unclear action.

items.label: Where is it?
items.detail: Identify the page, section, and relevant viewport.

items.label: Why does it matter?
items.detail: Explain the effect on readability, trust, or use.

items.label: What should change?
items.detail: Propose one concrete adjustment that can be checked.

figures.caption: The structured review format described in the post. Outcome scores are intentionally not charted.
